rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
(mc / t) proportional to the mean excess, under the same K
Same K and same interval: m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Same room is not enough if the cups have different surfaces.  ·  Equal times do not mean equal specific heats unless the masses and the intervals match.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Water equivalent W lets you write the calorimeter as an extra mass of water.  ·  Do not compare a covered cup with an open one.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Two liquids can be used to compare specific heats by cooling them in the same way. Identical conditions mean the same container shape, the same surface, the same room temperature, and the same temperature interval.  ·  Under those conditions the surface factor K is the same for both, and the excess temperature follows the same history. The time spent in that interval then depends on the heat capacity.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The law compares rates, not the final temperatures after an unlimited wait. Both end at room temperature.  ·  A lid or a fan changes K.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: From dθ/dt = −(K/mc) (θ − θ0), the time to pass between two temperatures is proportional to mc when K and the temperature limits are the same.  ·  Therefore m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2. The liquid that takes longer to cool through the same interval has the larger heat capacity.  ·  If the containers differ, K differs and the times cannot be compared by this relation. If the intervals differ, the excess temperatures differ and the relation again fails.
